deduction_checks: The subclass with F(u) in CPsh is a subsheaf and is closed under local uniform limits because F is uniformly continuous on local bounded ranges.
Smooth chain rule gives d'd''F(u)=F'(u)d'd''u+F''(u)d'u wedge d''u, positive for convex nondecreasing F.
The prescribed derivative 2t chi(t) has nonnegative derivative, is smooth across zero because chi vanishes nearby, and equals 2t beyond 1/2. An additive constant matches the square.
Addition uses closure separately in each variable; positive rescaling and adding constants preserve CPsh.
Local common shifts give positive CPsh f,g, their squares and their sum square. Algebra gives h^2=2f^2+2g^2-(f+g)^2 and polarization gives hl.
Each curvature of a square or product is a finite difference of positive closed currents; no arbitrary differentiation of order-zero currents is assumed to preserve order zero.
Continuous coefficients multiply differences of positive currents, so Gamma is well defined and independent of decompositions. Direct expansion proves symmetry and bilinearity.
On a neighborhood of each compact support, all four uniformly converging CPsh sequences and their limits have a common bounded positive shift.
Square and product curvature terms decompose into finitely many weakly convergent positive currents. CLD positive-current continuity applies separately to all coefficient products.
A fixed positive compact majorant bounds the masses of each positive sequence; finite sums give uniform local variation control, including additional uniformly converging continuous multipliers.
For smooth inputs, the separate closedness of S removes derivatives of S and ordinary Leibniz gives the displayed symmetric gradient product.

The separate-variable argument needs no common smooth approximation sequence and does not identify CPsh with arbitrary current-positive continuous functions.
The smooth chain rules are correct.

For uniformly converging CPsh u_j, exp(Bu_j) converges locally uniformly and remains CPsh. Curvatures and energies, including their exponential coefficients, converge by Section 2 and positive-current continuity.
The subclass satisfying both identities is a subsheaf closed under uniform limits and contains smooth psh inputs. CPsh minimality gives the identities for all CPsh u.
Combining the two identities produces the coefficient z^(-1) without nonsmooth derivatives.

theta and eta are positive (1,1)-forms and their nonnegative weighted products are positive.

Order-zero coefficient pairings converge by uniform coefficient control. Transferring two derivatives from dd(uS) to compact C^2 tests defines the same limit because S is order zero and u is bounded on the compact neighborhood.

deduction_checks: Young applied to the Radon–Nikodym densities with a=r^(l/2)/sqrt(z) and b=b_k*l*sqrt(z)*r^((l-2)/2) gives exactly (6.3).
Every weight is bounded and continuous on the common compact support; z is bounded below, V is smooth, and r=0 annihilates every term outside U.
The term -z*ddV*beta_k*S is nonpositive because ddV, beta_k and S have the requisite positivity.
The remaining coefficients are b_k*l and b_k*l*((b_k-1)*l+1). For k<n these are 2l and 2l(l+1); for k=n they are l and l.
Both cases are bounded by c_k*beta_(k-1), with c_k=2l(l+1)/(l-1). Bounding z by its U supremum proves (6.5).
Continuity of u near compact K_delta makes exp(Bu) bounded above and below there. On U, exp(Bu)>=exp(-BM), where M=sup_U |u|.
Identity (3.3) and positivity imply (6.6). Multiplication by beta_k gives at least its first-summand energy contribution; the omitted energy contribution when k<n is nonnegative.
The first-summand energy equals the integral in (6.5) by (4.4). Subtraction therefore cancels it exactly and gives c_k*B^(-1)*exp(2BM).
Taking B=1/(2M) gives 4e*l*(l+1)/(l-1)*M. If M=0, locality makes dd(uS) vanish on U, while beta_k annihilates its complement.
The recursion starts at J_0. The product of the factors (j+a)/(j+a-1) telescopes to (k+a)/a, yielding the alternative constant.

deduction_checks: A symmetric current pairs to zero with the antisymmetric part of alpha, including after multiplying by scalar test functions.

On a local ambient affine presentation the symmetric coefficient matrix of alpha is bounded on the compact support. The coefficient matrix of (dd||t||^2)^(n-m) is positive definite in the ambient space.
A sufficiently large scalar C gives positive-form inequalities plus/minus alpha<=C*(ddv)^(n-m), which remain valid under pullback even where the presentation has deficient rank.
Pairing with the positive mixed current gives -mu<=nu<=mu and therefore |nu|<=mu. Applying the n-factor case with repeated v proves integrability for |nu|.
For m=0 this uses only the repeated smooth v factors; for m=n alpha is a bounded local scalar. A finite partition of unity covers compact supports.
Goodness supplies arbitrarily small affinoid neighborhoods, and rational domains with positive real radii give refinements W inside Int(A).
As mu decreases to 1, the compact sets W_mu decrease to W. If each met A outside Int(A), compactness would force W to meet that complement, a contradiction.
No common zero of f_i,g implies W_mu misses {g=0}. Thus W_mu is contained in the ordinary open Y=Int(A) intersect {g!=0}.

Even product-kernel convolution of max is smooth, convex and coordinatewise increasing. Jensen gives the lower bound max and kernel support gives the upper bound max+epsilon. A coordinate lower than the maximum by more than 2epsilon never maximizes after convolution and is ignored.

The constant a_0=-1 guarantees a finite maximum even when every f_i vanishes. Near each zero its log coordinate is ignored, making rho ordinary smooth. The other coordinates are log norms of analytic units; convex composition gives smooth psh.
At x, max(a_0,...,a_s)<=0, so rho(x)<=epsilon-t/2<0. If rho<=t/4 then every a_i<=3t/4, hence the sublevel lies in W_exp(3t/4), a compact subset of Y. It is closed there and therefore compact.
For the abstract relatively compact negative-sublevel assumption, shift by c>0 with rho(x)+c<0 and choose 0<delta<c. Then the new closed sublevel lies in the old negative sublevel and is compact.

deduction_checks: Locally the ideal of Z is not contained in any prime of an n-dimensional irreducible component. Finite prime avoidance gives f in that ideal but outside all those primes. Its zero set has dimension<n.

CLD 15.2.1(b) puts every compact smooth (n,n)-form support in the complement of {f=0}. The continuous real function log|f| is bounded on each such compact support, giving canonical local integrability.
For F=max(t,0) convolved with an even compact smooth kernel, convexity and 0<=F'<=1 hold, with F=0 for t<=-1 and F=t for t>=1.
Each F_p(log|f|) is constant -p on an ordinary neighborhood of {f=0}, and is a smooth convex function of a log-unit elsewhere. It is therefore smooth psh throughout.
The derivative with respect to p is -1+F'(t+p)<=0. For finite t the expression eventually equals t; at zeros it is -p. The sequence decreases to log|f| on a fixed neighborhood.
Section 7 applies to this stage-one locally approchable pole and every full-CPsh mixed trace; its polar set contains Z. No unknown current is pulled back or classified.
Boundarylessness is used in Stokes and closedness of delta_X. Local differential separation is used for local positive-current sheaves, compact majorants and Radon measures.
Compact K_delta, neighborhood domains, a>=4 and smooth V supply the fixed compact C^2 integration-by-parts framework.
Full CPsh minimality supplies all closure arguments; local smooth approximation is assumed only for the polar function V, and explicitly constructed for log|f|.
Canonical integrability is used precisely in the final beta_0 bound; local sublevels turn the weighted integral into local integrability.

Goodness and separation support the analytic affinoid barrier construction; pure dimension gives the lower-dimensional zero set. Strictness is an allowed stronger analytic hypothesis and is not needed separately in the elementary barrier construction.
The weighted estimate is proved independently of CLD 8.4.3. The stronger full-CPsh polar conclusion is not inferred from the source theorem, which assumes local approchability of the u_i.
